On the left is a ribbed motor whose axis runs east-west. On the right is a domed pump housing held on with bolts. A terminal box sits on top of the motor, with a small brass-rimmed pressure gauge and a grey pressure-switch box above the housing. Under it all is a dark moulded base. Threaded nipples come out of all four sides and join white PVC pipe stubs through collar rings, and the stubs run to the canvas edges at N, E, S and W.
observed.south.png: The same picture without the label, on a clean transparent background with no shadow or backdrop. The pump body fills about the middle 60% of the canvas. The pipe stubs are about 70 px wide on a 512 px canvas. The view is a three-quarter overhead: you can see the tops of the terminal box, the switch and the base plus their front faces. The open threaded outlet on top points up toward the viewer and shows a dark bore. The rendering is painterly and fairly detailed.
observed.scale.png: The pump on its 1x1 footprint, outlined in yellow, beside a vanilla colonist. The body sits inside the cell and the stubs reach the cell edges. It reads as a small machine about knee-to-waist high next to the human.
observed.siblings.png: Reference set: a white poly horizontal tank, a tall green poly tank, an IBC cage tank and a red hose reel. They are painterly, realistic consumer and commercial plastics with dark fittings.
observed.assembled_1.png: In-game crop on dirt. A white tank on the left has a black port, a silver camlock coupler and a tan hose collar. A tan hose strand comes down from the top. The pump's north white stub rises and draws over the lower edge of the silver hose coupler/collar, ending there without joining anything. On the west, a neighbouring cream pipe meets the pump's west stub at a collar; that pipe is visibly wider than the pump's stub, and its end cap overlaps the collar. On the east, a thinner white pipe with a flanged union continues off to the right. The south stub runs down out of the frame. A yellow unpowered glyph covers the pump body.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same scene at a smaller zoom (about standard play). The pump reads as a dark compact machine with white pipes in four directions. The yellow unpowered bolt dominates the body. The north stub again overlaps the hose coupler area.
observed.assembled_3.png: A closer crop of the same scene. The pump's north white stub is drawn on top of the silver hose coupler and tan hose collar, which run east-west above it. observed.siblings.png: Reference parts: a white horizontal poly tank with black ports and a blue valve, a tall dark-green poly tank, an IBC tote in a galvanised cage, and a small red fire-hose reel. observed.facings.png: A labelled preview of the 4x4 link atlas on a checkerboard background. It shows thin off-white pipes: straights, 90° elbows with socket collars at both ends, tees and crosses with a socket at each arm, rounded end caps, and a short double-capped segment. Everything is drawn flat from above, with a soft cylindrical highlight along each pipe.
observed.south.png: The same atlas at full resolution on real alpha. The pipes are clean off-white or ivory with a light grey outline and soft shading. Fittings are slightly wider sockets with a rim line. The cross and tee hubs carry a small '+' seam mark. End caps are domed. There is no backdrop and no shadow.
observed.scale.png: The atlas tile shown inside a 1-cell yellow outline on brown ground, beside a vanilla pawn. The pipes look like thin white lines, roughly a seventh of a cell wide. They are clearly much thinner than the pawn's body and read as a small ground pipe.
observed.siblings.png: The reference family. A white poly horizontal tank with grey straps and a black lid, a dark green tall poly tank, an IBC cage tote and a red fire-hose reel. The materials look like realistic consumer or commercial products.
observed.assembled_1.png: An in-game close-up of a T-shaped run on dirt. The horizontal pipe has domed caps at both ends and a capped vertical branch going north. The junction fitting is a hub with sockets on three arms. It shows a '+' mark and a short rounded lobe that sticks out south below the horizontal pipe, where a tee has no arm. Faint lighter bands show at segment ends (near the left cap and the upper vertical). The material reads as white PVC.
observed.assembled_2.png: An in-game close-up of a long horizontal run with two tees: a north branch on the left and a south branch on the right. Each tee hub again shows a small lobe on its closed side: below the pipe on the left tee, above it on the right. The sockets are crisp and the pipe is even and white.
observed.assembled_3.png: An in-game horizontal pipe broken by white bolted flanges. Each flange has a wider short sleeve beside it, on one side only. A rusty, perforated steampunk-style valve wheel or dome sits on the pipe. The flanges and the valve do not appear in the candidate atlas, so they look like separate overlay parts (joint or valve) drawn on top of the candidate pipe.
observed.assembled_4.png: An in-game overview scene. A white poly tank on the left feeds a dark pump that has the yellow unpowered glyph. A white PVC main runs east past small rust-coloured valves and bolted flanges to a cross-shaped network: a north branch ends at a tan hose coupler, and a south branch ends in a domed cap. On the right, an elbow and riser climb up to the second tank's side port. The pipe reads as thin white PVC at this zoom. The pump's spigot looks noticeably fatter than the pipe. At the north branch, the hose coupler sits on the pipe partway along it, and the pipe carries on past the coupler to a cap.

CAMERA.seen: The card defines this part as strictly top-down (a ground-lying network), and the atlas is drawn flat from above with cylindrical shading. That suits a ground pipe under this card's description, and it matches in game.

BORE.seen: No open bore shows anywhere. Every terminus is a domed end cap, and elbows and sockets are drawn closed.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_4 the pipe meets the right tank's side port through an elbow and riser, and the left pump spigot is in line with the pipe. At the north branch the hose coupler sits on the pipe and the pipe runs on past it to a cap, so it is not clearly a terminal port. That is listed as a low-confidence finding.

LAYERS.seen: Valves, flanges and the hose coupler all draw over the pipe, and the pipe draws under the tanks and pump. Nothing that should be behind appears in front.

ROTATIONS.seen: There is one atlas, with all link pieces in the same white PVC palette, outline and thickness.

SIGNATURE.seen: Straights, elbows, crosses and end caps are all recognisable PVC socket fittings. However, the tee junctions use a hub with a lobe on the closed side (assembled_1 south lobe; assembled_2 lobes above and below), so a tee reads as a cross with one arm stubbed off rather than as a socket tee.

MATERIAL.seen: The off-white colour has a soft satin highlight and grey edge shading, and it reads as white PVC plastic rather than paint.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The pipe is centred in its cell at about 0.136 cell thick in scale.png and in game. It does not overflow.

ALPHA.seen: The background is clean transparent alpha in south.png, with no ground patch or shadow, and in game the dirt shows through.

OURS.seen: The PVC socket-fitting style is generated and is not vanilla or another mod's conduit art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: It is no longer enamel red. It is white Schedule-40-style PVC, a real-world consumer or commercial product that fits the 'modern consumer/commercial' note. The connector-size note is about the pumps, not this pipe.

LEGIBLE.seen: In assembled_4, at roughly standard zoom, the network reads clearly as thin white pipe lines with visible junctions and caps.
